span.label: AP is built on the precision-recall curve, and precision and recall trade against each other - detecting more objects raises recall and produces more false positives - so the single number is an area under a curve, not a count
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: what counts as a correct detection at all is set by an IoU threshold, and COCO averages over a RANGE of thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95 - so the definition of `correct` is itself a parameter being averaged over
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TWO NAMES FOR ONE THING: `average precision (AP), TRADITIONALLY CALLED mean average precision (mAP)`, and `THE COCO DATASET MAKES NO DISTINCTION BETWEEN AP AND mAP`. The review has to declare which word it will use before it can use it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND ONE NAME FOR TWO COMPUTATIONS: `The AP is computed differently in the VOC and in the COCO datasets` - 11-point interpolation over 20 categories at one IoU threshold, against 101-point interpolation over 80 categories averaged over ten IoU thresholds
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE CONSEQUENCE IS STATED PLAINLY AND IT IS ABOUT COMPARABILITY: `the differences in AP calculation MAKE IT HARD TO DIRECTLY COMPARE the performance of object detection models across the two datasets`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the improvements the field reports are quoted in that same word - 2.3 points from simOTA, 2.4 from stronger augmentation - so the increments inherit whatever the number means on the day
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the review derives AP separately for each dataset convention before reporting any model's score, rather than treating the metric as given
span.note: eliminates: a reader lining up a YOLOv2 number against a YOLOv5 number - the first is VOC AP and the second is COCO AP, and they are different quantities · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the naming collision is settled explicitly - `in the rest of this paper, we will refer to this metric as AP` - instead of the two words being used interchangeably
span.note: eliminates: a review whose own text is ambiguous about which of two names it means, in a document whose whole purpose is to compare numbers · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether the reported per-version gains are comparable to one another
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the gains are quoted in AP points and the review has just shown AP is two computations, so a 2.3-point gain and a 2.4-point gain are only comparable if both were measured under the same convention, which the review does not state per gain · outcome: absent-not-in-staged-text

span.label: AP / mAP - THE SAME QUANTITY UNDER TWO NAMES, and the review says so in its own first metrics sentence. `Traditionally called mean average precision`; COCO makes no distinction; the paper picks `AP` by fiat. A FIELD'S CENTRAL METRIC WITH AN UNSETTLED NAME

span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
